note: Two approved traces are sources: done/fixtures/houses/traced-house and done/fixtures/houses/unit1-house. HR-001 to HR-009 were authored from one reference plan, the traced house; Unit 1 widened their ranges and connections (garage, deck, folding doors, open links between halls) and introduced HR-010 to HR-013. Every range and every allowed connection is what the traces hold, widened to what a house plausibly holds, so each rule is exploratory until more plans are traced.

rules.name: kinds-known
rules.subject: every space
rules.rationale: Counts, areas and connections are judged by kind, so a space of no known kind is judged by nothing.

rules.name: edges-name-spaces
rules.subject: every edge that is not to the exterior
rules.rationale: An edge to nothing is a graph that was not read right.
exceptions: an edge marked exterior goes outside and is skipped

rules.name: kind-counts
rules.subject: each kind
rules.rationale: A house has a kitchen and a bedroom and not twenty porches; the ranges come from one plan.
exceptions: a kitchen that is also the dining space has no dining space of its own
rules.provenance: traced-house: 2 bedrooms, 3 closets, 1 each of bath, hall, living, kitchen, laundry, utility, porch, library

rules.name: kind-areas
rules.subject: each space
rules.predicate: has an area in square metres
rules.rationale: Areas widen what the one traced plan holds to what rooms of that kind plausibly measure.
rules.provenance: traced-house: bedrooms 9.30 and 13.40 m2, closets 0.80 to 2.91, bath 4.34, hall 2.92, living 14.46, kitchen 17.25, laundry 0.77, utility 0.82, porch 6.09, library 2.69

rules.name: connections-allowed
rules.subject: each door or open edge
rules.predicate: joins a pair of kinds by a means
rules.rationale: Which kinds open into each other, and by swing door, sliding door or open edge, as the traced plan does.
exceptions: the closet off the kitchen, by a sliding door, is in the traced plan
rules.provenance: traced-house: 13 links; unit1-house: folding doors of robes, linen and laundry, open links between halls and to a walk-in robe, a garage off the entry hall and a deck by sliding doors. Double-swing is swing, double-sliding is sliding; fixed is not listed

rules.name: closet-one-door
rules.subject: a closet
rules.object: one way in (a door or an open edge) and one neighbour
rules.rationale: A closet is entered from one room by one door, or is open to it as a walk-in robe is. Which rooms it may open off is the connection table's.
exceptions: the traced entry closet opens off the kitchen, not off a bedroom or a hall: the rule counts and the connection table allows it
rules.provenance: traced-house; unit1-house: the walk-in robe is joined to its bedroom by an open edge

rules.name: porch-off-living
rules.subject: a porch
rules.object: a living, kitchen or dining space
rules.rationale: A porch is a threshold to the shared rooms, not to a private or service one.
rules.provenance: traced-house: the porch opens into the living room

rules.name: bedroom-reach
rules.subject: every bedroom
rules.object: without passing through a bedroom or a bath
rules.rationale: One does not cross a bedroom or a bath to reach another bedroom.
exceptions: a graph with no entry reaches nothing and fails

rules.name: entry-space
rules.subject: the entry
rules.rationale: A house is entered into a shared or circulation space.
exceptions: the traced house is entered through its kitchen
rules.provenance: traced-house: the entry is the kitchen

rules.name: garage-off-circulation
rules.subject: every garage
rules.predicate: is reached from the entry without passing through a bedroom or a bath
rules.object: and is next to a hall or the entry space
rules.rationale: A garage is a way in from the car; it opens off the entry or a hall, never through a private room.
exceptions: a house with no garage has nothing to judge
rules.provenance: unit1-house: the garage opens off the entry hall

rules.name: deck-off-shared
rules.subject: a deck
rules.object: a living, kitchen or dining space, by at least one sliding door
rules.rationale: A deck is the shared rooms' outdoor extension, entered through sliding doors, not a private or service room's.
exceptions: a house with no deck has nothing to judge
rules.provenance: unit1-house: the deck is reached by sliding doors from the living and the dining

rules.name: folding-door
rules.subject: a folding door between two spaces
rules.predicate: joins a closet or a laundry
rules.object: to a bedroom or a hall
rules.rationale: Folding doors close robes, linen and laundry cupboards; they are not rooms' doors.
exceptions: a folding door to the outside (a garage door) joins no two spaces and is not judged

rules.name: hall-reach
rules.subject: every hall
rules.object: without passing through a bedroom or a bath
rules.rationale: A house with an entry hall and a bedroom hall opens one into the other, so the bedrooms are reached through circulation.
exceptions: a graph with no entry reaches nothing and fails
rules.provenance: unit1-house: the entry hall opens into the hall of the bedroom wing
